items.title: The Fed is expected to hike on Sep 16 - its first since 2023
items.detail: August core CPI rose 0.3% m/m against 0.2% prior and headline hit 3.4% y/y versus 3.3% expected. Prediction markets moved to 81-90% odds of a 25bp hike at the Sep 16 FOMC. Chair Warsh said at Jackson Hole that underlying inflation has not meaningfully improved. The 2-year closed at 4.63% and the 10-year at 4.96%.

items.title: Oil is carrying a geopolitical premium that can vanish on a headline
items.detail: Brent gained 8.7% on the week and WTI 9.4% on Strait of Hormuz supply fear, then fell 2.5% on Friday to just under $105 on hopes that diplomatic talks could improve shipping. Energy was the best sector for a second straight week - which means the book's energy weight is exposed to a single diplomatic outcome.

items.title: AI capex is concentrated in a handful of buyers
items.detail: The week's entire growth leadership traced to one event: Oracle reaffirming roughly $95bn of AI capex on Sep 10. Dell's $95.0bn AI-server backlog, HPE's raised FY26 guidance and the networking rotation all depend on a small number of buyers continuing to spend. DELL +11.98%, HPE +12.44% and SMCI +7.28% on a single day's news.

items.title: The AI-power trade has decoupled from AI capex
items.detail: On the biggest AI-capex news week of the year, CEG fell 0.43%, VST sits only 11.9% above its 52-week low and CCJ fell 0.76%. UBS cut NuScale to Sell with a $6 target on slow build timelines, roughly $700m of cumulative cash burn to 2028 and a lack of firm customer commitments; SMR fell 15.67%. The market is repricing nuclear from story to schedule.

items.title: Refining margins are at a generational extreme
items.detail: The WTI 3-2-1 crack spread cleared $64 a barrel, the highest since the 2022 disruptions and more than three times its $19 long-run median. VLO, PSX, PBF, MPC, DINO and DK all hit 52-week highs. Spreads at 3.4x their median mean-revert; the question is when, not whether.

items.title: Healthcare and medtech keep making new lows in a rising market
items.detail: BSX closed at 42.98, 1.8% above its 52-week low and 59.3% below its high, despite an August insider cluster at $48.26. UNH fell 2.37% and ISRG sits 38.9% below its high, only 12.4% above its low. On a day the S&P rose 0.86%, healthcare could not participate.

items.title: VIX at 15.84 going into an FOMC that may hike
items.detail: The VIX fell 11.21% on Friday to 15.84, which prices very little event risk two trading days before a decision that prediction markets put at 81-90% likely to be a hike. Cheap options are a hedging opportunity and a complacency signal at the same time.
